name: HyperEVM Testnet
limits: This is a private copy of HyperEVM Testnet: transactions confirm on the copy only and never appear on Hyperliquid testnet or its explorers.
Testnet prices, books and balances are testnet's own and thin: an order fills against a testnet book and a testnet HYPE price.
The copy keeps chain id 998, so a transaction signed for it is also valid on HyperEVM Testnet. Use test keys only.

The engine is Foundry anvil v1.8.5 behind chainsim's proxy, which mines one block per transaction: 3,000,000 gas for a small-block sender and 30,000,000 for one set to big blocks with chainsim set <name> hypercore big-blocks. A big block comes at least 60 s after the last one, so the fork's clock jumps forward to it. Blocks are mined on demand rather than every second, gas prices follow anvil's base fee, eth_bigBlockGasPrice answers the fixed 0.1 gwei measured on mainnet and testnet, and eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber is not served.

HyperCore is a local model chainsim keeps on the copy, not Hyperliquid's engine. up seeds the L1 block number, mark and oracle prices and asset info for the BTC, ETH, SOL and HYPE perps, token info for USDC and HYPE (token 1105 on testnet), spot info and spot price for HYPE/USDC, and one order book per seeded perp. Spot balance, position, withdrawable and margin summary reads answer from the copy's Core state for any user, with zeros for an account that has none. Any other query reverts with a chainsim reason until chainsim set <name> precompile seeds it.

The fork's RPC and WebSocket addresses are chainsim's proxy, which applies CoreWriter actions and bridge transfers after each block, for any client over HTTP or WebSocket. Subscriptions are anvil's own. A read inside the block of an action never sees its effect.

Other clients' requests to the proxy wait while a chainsim command changes HyperCore state: the catch-up every command runs first, and each step of a command. Commands read the info API and the upstream before they take the lock, except set hypercore book --live, which reads the info API under it (about 0.4 s). time --replay takes the lock one candle at a time and set hypercore mirror in three steps, so a request waits at most one step (about 0.4 s for a mirror of 177 positions), and a transaction sent between steps is applied by the next one.

The proxy's /info answers clearinghouseState, spotClearinghouseState, openOrders, userFills, meta, metaAndAssetCtxs, l2Book, allMids, borrowLendUserState, borrowLendReserveState and allBorrowLendReserveStates from the copy's state, with the dex argument for builder-deployed dexes the copy tracks, and refuses other request types with HTTP 422. Asset contexts of perps the copy does not track are the snapshot from up, and allMids covers perps only.

Modeled actions are limit orders on perps (GTC, IOC and ALO) matched against the order book snapshot and other orders resting on the copy, cancels by order id and by client order id, spot sends, USD class transfers, sendAsset of USDC between perp dexes and spot, borrow and lend supply and withdraw, and the account abstraction. Other actions are recorded and decoded with no effect, so spot orders, vault transfers, staking and delegation change nothing.

Market rules are simplified. Fees are the base tier (0.045% taker, 0.015% maker) with no volume tiers, discounts or rebates. Margin follows each perp's margin tiers from the info API meta, and the tier of a position is taken from its notional. A liquidation closes every position of the account at the mark price at once, with no partial or backstop step, and a negative balance after it is reset to zero. Funding is paid every hour of the fork's clock. Perps that are isolated only hold isolated margin per position, set at open from the order's leverage. updateIsolatedMargin is a signed exchange action on Hyperliquid, the copy offers it as chainsim set <name> hypercore isolated-margin, and no CoreWriter action changes isolated margin. The delay the network applies to orders is not modeled.

Prices move only through chainsim set <name> hypercore price and chainsim time <name> --replay. Resting orders fill when such a move crosses them, not when the book changes, and the L1 block number keeps its value from up. A replay mines one block per hourly candle, an hour apart from the fork's current time rather than at the candles' own dates.

Funding rates come from the last settled rate in fundingHistory at up, or the current rate from the info API for perps added later, and stay fixed until chainsim set <name> hypercore funding changes them. Builder-deployed (HIP-3) perps set their rate each hour from the premium of the copy's book at that moment rather than an hourly average, with the funding multiplier, interest rate and clamp perpDexs gave when the perp was added. A HIP-3 perp with no book on the copy keeps its rate, and a rate set with chainsim set <name> hypercore funding replaces the formula.

Order books are snapshots from the Hyperliquid info API, taken at up or by chainsim set <name> hypercore book <coin> --live, and fills on the copy consume their depth. They do not follow the live market.

HYPE sent to 0x2222…2222 and a linked ERC-20 sent to its token system address credit HyperCore spot on the copy. A spot send to a system address credits the sender's EVM balance directly, with no system transaction. The CoreDepositWallet path for USDC is not modeled.

set hypercore mirror copies a testnet account's perp positions and margin on the main dex and on every builder-deployed dex it has value on (isolated positions with their margin), its spot balances, its borrow and lend positions and its account abstraction from the info API as they are at that moment, and its HYPE and profile token balances on the EVM side.

Builder-deployed (HIP-3) perps are tracked once set hypercore book, price or mirror names one, and none are seeded by default. Each dex has its own USD balance and cross margin, moved in and out with sendAsset, and only dexes with USDC collateral trade.

Borrow and lend follows the documented stablecoin rate (0.05 + 4.75 x max(0, utilization - 0.8) a year) indexed hourly and LTVs from up. A collateral token's price is the median of its spot price and the mark and oracle price of the perp on the same asset, with the USDT to USDC conversion taken as 1, and moves with chainsim set <name> hypercore price on either. Stablecoin prices and the rates of tokens that are not stablecoins stay at their value from up. Borrowing is implicit for portfolio margin and unified accounts on a spot debit and a credit repays first. Past the documented portfolio margin ratio of 0.95 the backstop takes 20% of each collateral at a time until the account is healthy: the full-liquidation threshold and any penalty are not published, so the copy always steps by 20%. Supply and borrow caps are not modeled.

The default public upstream answers every state read at its latest block, whatever block the read names. up --block with it exits 7, and set CHAINSIM_HYPEREVM_TESTNET_RPC to an archive provider URL to fork at an older block.
Accounts and storage the copy has not written are read from the upstream on first access, at the upstream's latest state, so a long session can read state newer than the fork block.

The default upstream allows 100 requests per minute per IP. up makes about 103 requests, so set CHAINSIM_HYPEREVM_TESTNET_RPC to a provider URL for heavier runs. The Hyperliquid testnet info API takes 11 requests at up, and CHAINSIM_HYPERLIQUID_TESTNET_INFO replaces its URL.
App indexers and explorers read the public chain, so they do not show what happens on the copy.
